title: Display Your Face at Tokyo's Shibuya Scramble
paragraphs: Shibuya Scramble Crossing in Tokyo is one of the most famous places in Japan. Huge numbers of people cross the street there at the same time, and there are giant video screens on the buildings around it. Now, tourists may soon be able to see their own faces on one of these screens.

The idea comes from Tokyu, a Japanese railway and property company. From July 24 to 26, 2026, it tested a new service with the temporary name "Shibuya Scramble Crossing Photo." During the test, photos of 48 travelers from countries such as Germany, India, Italy, Korea, the US and Vietnam were shown on Q's Eye, a large video screen on the side of the QFRONT building. Each photo was shown for 15 seconds. The travelers' faces appeared inside a picture of Hachiko, the famous loyal dog whose statue stands near Shibuya Station.

Participants are told in advance when their photo will appear, so they can be ready to take pictures and videos. They do not need to stand in the busy crossing, because they can photograph the screen from the plaza next to the Hachiko statue.

Tokyu plans to start the service officially in March 2027. It is expected to cost between 5,000 and 10,000 yen. In the future, users may be able to choose a time online and upload a photo of their face. At the moment, people have to wait six days for their photo to be shown, but Tokyu wants to make this shorter, and maybe even offer same-day service.

The company is also thinking about other ideas. For example, users may be able to add personal messages on the screen or buy goods showing their photo on the screen. The service is mainly for foreign tourists, but anyone will be able to use it.
